The manic/mixed episode distinction in bipolar disorder patients appears to suggest that these episodes are relatively stable across time. Studies have found that diagnostic stability for manic and mixed episodes in patients with bipolar disorder does occur over time, indicating a pattern of consistent diagnoses. However, it is essential to note that the reliability and consistency of these diagnoses can vary depending on several factors, such as the specific study design, population, and criteria used.

In other words, while there may be some degree of stability in the diagnosis of manic/mixed episodes over time for certain patients with bipolar disorder, it's not a universal characteristic that applies to all individuals within this condition. It is also worth mentioning that the distinction between manic and mixed episodes can sometimes be challenging to make due to overlapping symptoms and differences in diagnostic criteria.

To further explore this topic, more research studies are necessary to understand the nuances of diagnosing and managing bipolar disorder in various populations over time.
